paras.text: 4. Standard of Deferred Payments (Standard of a Deferred Payments)
paras.urdu: 4۔ آئندہ ادائیگیوں کا معیار: (Standard of a Deferred Payments)
paras.pashto: 4. د راتلونکو تادیو معیار (Standard of a Deferred Payments)

paras.text: In the present age giving and taking on credit has become necessary, e.g. small shopkeepers take goods on credit from wholesalers and pay the sum after some time. Therefore for this purpose it is necessary to adopt such a measure that neither party has to bear undue profit or loss. This purpose is fulfilled with the help of money, because stability to a great extent is found in the quantity of money; therefore, instead of any other thing, credit is taken and given in the form of money.
paras.urdu: دورِ حاضر میں ادھار دینا اور لینا ضروری ہو گیا ہے۔ مثلاً چھوٹے دکاندار تھوک فروشوں سے ادھار مال لیتے ہیں اور کچھ مدت کے بعد رقم ادا کرتے ہیں۔ چنانچہ اس مقصد کے لیے ایسی تدبیر کرنا لازمی ہے۔ جس سے دونوں فریقوں کو ناجائز نفع یا نقصان نہ اٹھانا پڑے یہ مقصد زر کی مدد سے پورا ہو جاتا ہے، کیونکہ زر کی مقدار میں بڑی حد تک استحکام پایا جاتا ہے اس لیے کسی اور شے کی بجائے زر کی شکل میں ادھار لیا اور دیا جاتا ہے۔

paras.text: 5. Means of Transferring Value
paras.urdu: 5۔ انتقالِ قدر کا ذریعہ: (Means of Transferring Value)
paras.pashto: 5. د ارزښت د لېږد وسیله (Means of Transferring Value)

paras.text: Through money it becomes easy for us to transfer our movable or immovable property (which cannot be moved, e.g. land, house or shop) from one place to another. Its method is that we first sell such property and obtain rupees, and then with the help of these rupees buy similar property at the other place where we want to transfer the property.

paras.text: 6. Means of Government Payment and Receipts
paras.urdu: 6۔ سرکاری ادائیگیوں اور وصولیوں کا ذریعہ: (Means of Government Payment and Receipts)
paras.pashto: 6. د دولتي تادیو او وصولیو وسیله (Means of Government Payment and Receipts)

paras.text: Government payments and receipts too take place through money, e.g. the government collects tax, duty, revenue and fines etc. in the form of money, and gives payments, e.g. salaries, pensions, stipends and prizes etc., in the form of money.
paras.urdu: سرکاری ادائیگیاں اور وصولیاں بھی زر کی معرفت ہی ہوتی ہیں۔ مثلاً حکومت ٹیکس، محصول، مالیہ اور جرمانہ وغیرہ زر کی شکل میں وصول کرتی ہے۔ اور ادائیگیاں مثلاً تنخواہیں، پنشنیں، وظائف اور انعامات وغیرہ زر کی شکل میں دیتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: دولتي تادیې او وصولۍ هم د پیسو له لارې کېږي؛ لکه حکومت مالیه، محصول، د ځمکې مالیه او جریمه او نور د پیسو په بڼه اخلي او تادیې، لکه معاشونه، تقاعدونه، بورسونه او انعامونه او نور د پیسو په بڼه ورکوي.

paras.text: 7. A Unit of Account
paras.urdu: 7۔ حساب کی اکائی: (A Unit of Account)
paras.pashto: 7. د حساب واحد (A Unit of Account)

paras.text: Money is also used for accounts, because counting of sums is done with reference to it. The price of things is told and the account of goods and services is kept. For example, we say that the monthly income of such a person is Rs 10 thousand, the price of a motor car is five lakh rupees, the total wealth of such a man is two crore rupees. As it were, the rupee is such a unit in whose form accounts are kept.

paras.text: 8. Miscellaneous functions of money (Miscellaneous Function)
paras.urdu: 8۔ زر کے متفرق فرائض: (Miscellaneous Function)
paras.pashto: 8. د پیسو متفرقې دندې (Miscellaneous Function)

paras.pashto: له یادو دندو پرته (د بارټر پر ځای د پیسو په کارولو لاندې دندې هم ترسره کېږي)

paras.text: iii. Because the mobility of capital becomes easy, capital formation (Capital Formation) increases.

5. Means of Transferring Value

Through money it becomes easy for us to transfer our movable or immovable property (which cannot be moved, e.g. land, house or shop) from one place to another. Its method is that we first sell such property and obtain rupees, and then with the help of these rupees buy similar property at the other place where we want to transfer the property.

6. Means of Government Payment and Receipts

Government payments and receipts too take place through money, e.g. the government collects tax, duty, revenue and fines etc. in the form of money, and gives payments, e.g. salaries, pensions, stipends and prizes etc., in the form of money.

For example, we say that the monthly income of such a person is Rs 10 thousand, the price of a motor car is five lakh rupees, the total wealth of such a man is two crore rupees. As it were, the rupee is such a unit in whose form accounts are kept.

8. Miscellaneous functions of money (Miscellaneous Function)

Besides the above functions, (through the use of money instead of barter, the following functions are also performed)

i. Every consumer can make his satisfaction of want (Satisfaction) the maximum (Maximum).

ii. The process of saving and investment becomes easy.

iii. Because the mobility of capital becomes easy, capital formation (Capital Formation) increases.

iv. The exchange of things becomes easy, because of which trade flourishes at the national and international level.

v. Because of money the working of the price mechanism (Price Mechanism) becomes easy, and the allocation of productive resources for different purposes (Allocation of Resocurces) takes place in a better way.

vi. The functioning (Functioning) of the economic system (Economic System) becomes easy and firm.

However, this point is also worth considering: because of the use of money instead of barter, when the government prints more notes, the problem of inflation (Inflation) and dearness arises, by which the rich become richer and the poor poorer.

4. Standard of Deferred Payments (Standard of a Deferred Payments)

In the present age giving and taking on credit has become necessary, e.g. small shopkeepers take goods on credit from wholesalers and pay the sum after some time. Therefore for this purpose it is necessary to adopt such a measure that neither party has to bear undue profit or loss. This purpose is fulfilled with the help of money, because stability to a great extent is found in the quantity of money; therefore, instead of any other thing, credit is taken and given in the form of money.

5. Means of Transferring Value

Through money it becomes easy for us to transfer our movable or immovable property (which cannot be moved, e.g. land, house or shop) from one place to another. Its method is that we first sell such property and obtain rupees, and then with the help of these rupees buy similar property at the other place where we want to transfer the property.

6. Means of Government Payment and Receipts

Government payments and receipts too take place through money, e.g. the government collects tax, duty, revenue and fines etc. in the form of money, and gives payments, e.g. salaries, pensions, stipends and prizes etc., in the form of money.

7. A Unit of Account

Money is also used for accounts, because counting of sums is done with reference to it. The price of things is told and the account of goods and services is kept. For example, we say that the monthly income of such a person is Rs 10 thousand, the price of a motor car is five lakh rupees, the total wealth of such a man is two crore rupees. As it were, the rupee is such a unit in whose form accounts are kept.

8. Miscellaneous functions of money (Miscellaneous Function)

Besides the above functions, (through the use of money instead of barter, the following functions are also performed)

i. Every consumer can make his satisfaction of want (Satisfaction) the maximum (Maximum).

ii. The process of saving and investment becomes easy.

iii. Because the mobility of capital becomes easy, capital formation (Capital Formation) increases.

iv. The exchange of things becomes easy, because of which trade flourishes at the national and international level.

v. Because of money the working of the price mechanism (Price Mechanism) becomes easy, and the allocation of productive resources for different purposes (Allocation of Resocurces) takes place in a better way.

vi. The functioning (Functioning) of the economic system (Economic System) becomes easy and firm.

However, this point is also worth considering: because of the use of money instead of barter, when the government prints more notes, the problem of inflation (Inflation) and dearness arises, by which the rich become richer and the poor poorer.

The money thing should be such that every person can easily recognise the genuine and the counterfeit, as the value is written on different coins and notes, and fake coins and notes are easily recognised.

sections.content:
Qualities / Essentials of Good Money

Only that thing can do the best work for performing the function of money in which the following qualities are found.

1. General Acceptability

For the thing which is to be used as money it is necessary that it has general acceptability, so that every person is ready, without hesitation, to give his things in exchange for it. A metal obtains general acceptability because of its intrinsic quality, as gold or silver does; or because of the government’s law, as currency notes do; or because of trust, as the credit money (Credit Money) of banks. The thing which all people are not ready to accept cannot become money. In our country currency notes are used while buying and selling things, because every person accepts them with great pleasure. In contrast, if some person goes out for shopping and, to make payment, picks up the utensils of his house, then perhaps no shopkeeper would even give him goods, because utensils have no general acceptability as a medium of exchange.

2. Transferring Value

The thing should be such that is small in “volume” (Volume) and holds a large amount of value (Value), so that there is ease in handling, carrying, moving, taking and giving it. For this purpose gold, silver and currency notes can become the best money. In contrast, skins, arrows-and-bows or cattle cannot do the work of good money.

3. Durability

For the thing which becomes a medium of exchange it is necessary that it is durable, so that it can always maintain its value, like gold, silver and currency notes; milk and apples etc. cannot do this work.

4. Recognisability

The money thing should be such that every person can easily recognise the genuine and the counterfeit, as the value is written on different coins and notes, and fake coins and notes are easily recognised.

5. Divisibility (Divisability)

The money thing should be such that, if it is divided into small parts for buying goods of small value, no difference comes in its value. A large bar of gold can be divided into small pieces, and notes too are of different values, e.g. a note of one thousand rupees, of five hundred, of one hundred and of ten rupees. But if a cow, a chair or a goat were used for money, they could not be divided into small parts.

6. Manufacturing / formation

The thing of which money is made should be so soft that it can be cast in moulds and coins made of it, and the government can engrave some mark on it so that genuine and fake coins can be distinguished. Thus, besides coins, the value and the guarantee of the government are written on notes.

شے ایسی ہونی چاہیے جو کم ”حجم“ (Volume) میں زیادہ مقدار (Value) کی حامل ہو تاکہ اسے سنبھالنے اٹھائے پھرنے، منتقل کرنے اور لینے دینے میں آسانی رہے۔ اس مقصد کے لیے سونا چاندی اور کرنسی نوٹ بہترین زر بن سکتے ہیں۔ ان کے برعکس کھالیں، تیر کمان یا مویشی عمدہ زر کا کام نہیں دے سکتے۔

3۔ پائیداری: (Durability)

آلہ مبادلہ بننے والی شے کے لیے ضروری ہے کہ وہ پائیدار ہو، تاکہ وہ اپنی قدر و قیمت ہمیشہ برقرار رکھ سکے، جیسے سونا، چاندی، کرنسی نوٹ وغیرہ دودھ اور سیب یہ کام نہیں کر سکتے۔

4۔ شناخت پذیری: (Recognisability)

زر کی شے ایسی ہونی چاہیے جس کے کھرے اور کھوٹے کی پہچان ہر شخص کو آسانی سے ہو سکے۔ جیسے مختلف سکوں اور نوٹوں پر ان کی مالیت درج ہوتی ہے۔ اور جعلی سکوں اور نوٹوں کی پہچان بہ آسانی ہو جاتی ہے۔

5۔ تقسیم پذیری: (Divisability)

زر کی چیز ایسی ہونی چاہیے۔ کہ اگر تھوڑی قدر و قیمت والی اشیاء خریدنے کے لیے اسے چھوٹے چھوٹے حصوں میں تقسیم کیا جائے تو اس کی مالیت میں کوئی فرق نہ آئے۔ سونے کی ایک بڑی سلاخ کو تو چھوٹے چھوٹے ٹکڑوں میں تقسیم کیا جا سکتا ہے۔ اور نوٹ بھی مختلف مالیت کے ہوتے ہیں۔ مثلاً ہزار روپے کا، پانچ سو روپے کا سو روپے کا اور دس روپے کا نوٹ لیکن اگر زر کے لیے گائے یا کرسی یا بھیڑے کو استعمال کیا جاتا ہو تو انہیں چھوٹے حصوں میں تقسیم نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔

6۔ تشکیل پذیری: (Manufacturing / formation)

زر جس شے کا بنا ہو وہ اتنی نرم ہونی چاہیے کہ اسے سانچوں میں ڈھال کر اس کے سکے بنائے جا سکیں۔ اور حکومت اس پر کرید کر کوئی نشان ظاہر کر سکے تاکہ اصلی اور جعلی سکوں میں تمیز ہو سکے۔ چنانچہ سکوں کے علاوہ نوٹوں پر ان کی مالیت اور حکومت کی ضمانت درج ہوتی ہے۔
